image_query: Elephanta Caves Trimurti Sadashiva sculpture Shiva three faces
tweets: The Trimurti Sadāśiva of Elephanta — Śiva carved in three faces from a single basalt wall, 6th century CE. At center, Tatpuruṣa gazes serene; to his right, fierce Aghora; to his left, gentle Vāmadeva as Umā. Three aspects, one godhead: destroyer, creator, preserver.

Carved into basalt on Gharapuri island near Mumbai, the site got its colonial name when Portuguese sailors found a monolithic stone elephant by the shore and named it Elephanta. A UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987. Follow @yddoseOfHistory for your daily dose of history
